chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha', from Ahmad ibn 'Umar, from Abi al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the time of Zuhr and 'Asr. He said: The time of Zuhr is when the sun declines until the shadow goes a qamah, and the time of 'Asr is from one and a half qamahs until two qamahs.

key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, whose movement indicates prayer times
key_terms.الظِّلُّ: the shadow used as a sign for determining time
key_terms.قَامَةً: a measured bodily length used here as a shadow-length indicator
key_terms.قَامَتَيْنِ: two measured lengths indicating the later extent of the prayer time
key_terms.وَقْتِ: the prescribed time or period for an act of worship

ai.seo_question: What are the times of Zuhr and 'Asr prayer according to this hadith from al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding the timing of the Zuhr and 'Asr prayers based on the sun's decline and the measured length of shadow. It is significant in Shia fiqh for defining the prayer times through observable natural signs.
